ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\angle ABC=\angle FAC=90^\circ$, the length of $BC$ is $3\text{cm}$, the length of $AB$ is $4\text{cm}$, and the length of $AF$ is $12\text{cm}$. What is the area of the square $CDEF$ in $\text{cm}^2$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given in right triangle $\triangle ABC$, $AC= \sqrt{AB^{2}+BC^{2}}=\sqrt{3^{2}+4^{2}}=5\,\text{cm}$,
in right triangle $\triangle ACF$, $CF= \sqrt{AF^{2}+AC^{2}}=\sqrt{12^{2}+5^{2}}=13\,\text{cm}$,
$\therefore$ the area of square $CDEF$ is $13\times13=\boxed{169}\,\text{cm}^{2}$

In right triangle $\triangle ACF$, $CF=\sqrt{AF^{2}+AC^{2}}=\sqrt{12^{2}+5^{2}}=13\text{ cm}$. Therefore, the area of square $CDEF$ is $13\times13=\boxed{169}\text{ cm}^{2}$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the right side of the figure is a square labeled CDEF, with C at the lower left, D at the lower right, E at the upper right, and F at the upper left; therefore CF is one side of the square. On the left side of the square are connected points A, B, C, and F. Right-angle marks are drawn at B and A in the figure, corresponding to the given ∠ABC=90° and ∠FAC=90° in the problem. Reasoning: In right triangle ABC, AB=4 cm and BC=3 cm, so AC is the hypotenuse. By the Pythagorean theorem, AC=sqrt(4^2+3^2)=sqrt(16+9)=5 cm. Next look at right triangle ACF: ∠FAC=90°, AF=12 cm, and AC=5 cm, so CF is the hypotenuse. By the Pythagorean theorem, CF=sqrt(12^2+5^2)=sqrt(144+25)=sqrt(169)=13 cm. Since CF is the side length of square CDEF, the area of the square is 13^2=169 cm^2.
